title: StreamEvent
description:
One line of the `stream`/`watch` stdout wire protocol (v1). Every
`StatusField` result is wrapped in `Field` and carries the monotonic
`generation` of the check that produced it; each check is bracketed by
`CheckStarted`/`CheckComplete` with the same generation; `watch`
additionally emits `Heartbeat` for liveness and `Error` for a bad stdin
command or a probe failure. Every run's first line is `Hello`.

oneOf.title: Hello
oneOf.description:
First line of every `stream`/`watch` run — declares the protocol
version and (for `watch`) whether the config-change watcher started.

oneOf.title: CheckStarted
oneOf.description:
A check has begun; every following `Field` at this `generation`
belongs to it, until the matching `CheckComplete`.

token.description:
Echoed from `WatchCommand::RefreshToken`; `None` for any
non-command-triggered check.

oneOf.title: Field
oneOf.description: One probe result, tagged with its check's `generation`.

oneOf.title: CheckComplete
oneOf.description:
The check at this `generation` has finished (or been superseded —
either way its `Field` lines will not continue).

oneOf.title: Heartbeat
oneOf.description:
`watch`-only liveness marker, emitted on a fixed cadence regardless
of check activity.

oneOf.title: Error
oneOf.description:
A recoverable problem (`fatal: false` — e.g. an unrecognized stdin
command) or a terminal one (`fatal: true`).

CaptivePortalStatus.description:
Whether something between this machine and the internet is
intercepting plain HTTP traffic to serve a login page (a captive
portal), determined by fetching Apple's own hotspot-detect endpoint —
the same check macOS itself uses.

oneOf.title: Clear
oneOf.description:
The hotspot-detect request got the expected response — nothing is
intercepting traffic.

oneOf.title: Detected
oneOf.description:
The response was rewritten, redirected, or otherwise not what was
expected — something between this machine and the internet is
intercepting the request.

oneOf.title: Unknown
oneOf.description:
The probe didn't get a conclusive answer (e.g. the request itself
failed) — not evidence of a portal, just an inconclusive check.

ConnectResult.description: Result of a single TCP connect probe against a target host and port.

Interface.description: Observable status of a single network interface.

oneOf.title: Ipv4Only
oneOf.description: A routable IPv4 address, but no routable IPv6 address.

oneOf.title: Ipv6Only
oneOf.description: A routable IPv6 address, but no routable IPv4 address.

oneOf.title: DualStack
oneOf.description: A routable address in both families.

oneOf.title: None
oneOf.description:
No routable address in either family (link-local only, or no
address at all).

PingResult.description: Result of a single ping probe against a target host.

ProbeGroup.description:
Which target list a streamed `Ping`/`Connect` item, or a `GroupComplete`
marker, belongs to.

oneOf.title: Reachability
oneOf.description:
ICMP reachability of well-known public IPv4 anycast DNS resolvers
(see `DEFAULT_PING_TARGETS`).

oneOf.title: ReachabilityV6
oneOf.description:
Same as `Reachability`, but IPv6 targets (see
`DEFAULT_PING_TARGETS_V6`).

oneOf.title: GatewayReachability
oneOf.description:
ICMP reachability of the default gateway's IP(s) — a LAN-hop
signal, distinct from `Reachability`'s public anycast targets:
unreachable here alongside unreachable public targets points at the
local link rather than the ISP or upstream.

oneOf.title: NameserverReachability
oneOf.description:
ICMP reachability of each configured resolver's IP, probed directly
rather than inferred from whether name resolution succeeds.

oneOf.title: DomainReachability
oneOf.description:
TCP connect (port 443) reachability of well-known domains (see
`DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_TARGETS`) — a real connect rather than ICMP
ping, since some large operators filter ICMP at their edge
regardless of whether the service itself is up.

oneOf.title: NameserverConnect
oneOf.description:
TCP connect (port 53) reachability of each configured resolver's
IP. Like `DomainReachability`, this catches resolvers that filter
ICMP but still serve queries.

oneOf.title: Resolution
oneOf.description:
DNS resolution of well-known domains (see
`DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_TARGETS`).

ResolutionResult.description: Result of resolving a single domain name.

Resolver.description: A single resolver configuration, one per network service.

Scope.description:
How much of a check `StreamEvent::CheckStarted` is announcing — the wire
mirror of the CLI-internal `CheckScope`. `Full` re-probes everything;
`Confidence` runs only the confidence-determining probes (a poll-tick
safety-net check).

StatusField.description:
One probe's result, delivered as soon as that probe completes. For a
target-list probe (`Ping`/`Connect`/`Resolution`), that's per-target, not
per-group — a slow or unreachable target no longer holds up the rest of
its list from being visible (see `for_each_concurrent`). `GroupComplete`
marks a target list as fully drained; only sent for the four groups
`PartialStatus::confidence` needs a completeness signal for.

oneOf.title: Interfaces
oneOf.description: The current network interfaces.

oneOf.title: Vpn
oneOf.description:
VPN/tunnel status derived from the interface list and the primary
(default-route) interface.

oneOf.title: Resolvers
oneOf.description:
Every DNS resolver macOS knows about, including scoped
(per-interface) resolvers.

oneOf.title: SplitDns
oneOf.description:
Whether any resolver is scoped to a specific interface — the
mechanism VPN clients like Cisco AnyConnect use for split-DNS.

oneOf.title: Ping
oneOf.description: One target's ICMP ping result, for the given `group`.

oneOf.title: Connect
oneOf.description: One target's TCP connect result, for the given `group`.

oneOf.title: Resolution
oneOf.description:
One domain's DNS resolution result (always `ProbeGroup::Resolution`
— the only resolution group — so unlike `Ping`/`Connect` this isn't
tagged with one).

oneOf.title: GroupComplete
oneOf.description:
`group`'s target list has fully drained — every target in it has
sent its `Ping`/`Connect`/`Resolution` result at least once.

oneOf.title: Proxy
oneOf.description: The system's configured HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS/PAC proxy settings.

oneOf.title: WifiIdentity
oneOf.description:
SSID/connected-state — the slow half of Wi-Fi status
(`system_profiler`-backed).

oneOf.title: WifiRadio
oneOf.description:
Channel/signal/noise/security/PHY-mode — the fast half of Wi-Fi
status (CoreWLAN-backed, no shell-out).

oneOf.title: IpStack
oneOf.description:
Whether the machine has a routable IPv4 address, IPv6 address,
both, or neither.

oneOf.title: CaptivePortal
oneOf.description: Whether a captive portal was detected.

Trigger.description: Why a check started, carried by `StreamEvent::CheckStarted`.

oneOf.title: initial
oneOf.description: The first check of a `stream`/`watch` run.

oneOf.title: config_change
oneOf.description: An OS network-config change (interface up/down, IP/DNS reconfig, VPN).

oneOf.title: poll
oneOf.description: The adaptive-interval poll safety net.

oneOf.title: command
oneOf.description: A `WatchCommand` read from stdin.

VpnStatus.description:
VPN / tunnel status derived from the interface list and the primary
(default-route) interface.

routed_subnets.description:
Subnets routed through the VPN (its own assigned address/subnet,
plus any additional split-tunnel destinations it pushes), formatted
as CIDR strings. Empty when not connected, or when the dynamic
store's per-service IPv4 dict for the tunnel interface carries no
`AdditionalRoutes` — a full-tunnel VPN commonly has none, since it
becomes the default route (`OverridePrimary`) instead of pushing a
discrete route list.

WatcherState.description:
Whether the OS config-change watcher started, reported by
`StreamEvent::Hello`. `Unavailable` means `watch` degraded to poll-only
(e.g. `SCDynamicStore` setup rejected in a sandbox).

oneOf.title: disabled
oneOf.description:
No config-change watcher is run at all — the one-shot `stream`
subcommand, which does a single pass and exits.

WifiIdentity.description:
SSID/connected-state, the slow half of Wi-Fi status — only obtainable via
`system_profiler` (a ~1s shell-out), since reading it through CoreWLAN
needs Location Services authorization a bare CLI/TUI binary can't get.

WifiRadio.description:
Channel/signal/noise/security/PHY-mode, the fast half of Wi-Fi status —
read straight from CoreWLAN (`CWWiFiClient`/`CWInterface`), no shell-out.
